items.stem:
Assertion (A) : In humans, males play an important role in determining the sex of the child.
Reason (R) : Males have two X chromosomes.
items.assertion: In humans, males play an important role in determining the sex of the child.

options.label: A
options.text: Both assertion (A) and reason (R) are true and reason (R) is the correct explanation of assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both assertion (A) and reason (R) are true but reason (R) is not the correct explanation of assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true but reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false but reason (R) is true.

items.answer: (c) Assertion (A) is true but reason (R) is false. The sex of a child depends on the type of male gamete that fuses with the female gamete. Human beings possess 23 pairs of chromosomes; 22 pairs are autosomes and the remaining pair comprises the sex chromosomes - XX in females and XY in males - so a male does not have two X chromosomes. If an egg carrying an X chromosome fuses with a sperm carrying an X chromosome the child is a girl; if it fuses with a sperm carrying a Y chromosome the child is a boy.

items.answer: (a) Both assertion (A) and reason (R) are true and reason (R) is the correct explanation of assertion (A). Traits which develop in the life time of an individual and do not pass to the progeny are called acquired traits; learning a skill such as dance or music, loss of body parts and change in weight are examples of acquired traits.

items.answer: (c) Assertion (A) is true but reason (R) is false. Eye colour and height are genetically inherited traits, as these are expressed by genes. Inherited traits are the traits which are transferred from parents to young ones, whereas acquired traits are the characters acquired by an individual during its lifetime and cannot be inherited.
